p: let us lay aside every weight: An applying of the former examples, by which we ought to be stirred up to run the whole race, casting away all hindrances and impediments.
doth so easily beset us: For sin besieges us on all sides, so that we cannot escape.
He sets before us, as the mark of this race, Jesus himself our captain, who willingly overcame all the roughness of the same way.
Looking unto Jesus the author and: As it were upon the mark of our faith.
joy that was set before him: While he had every type of blessedness in his hand and power, yet suffered willingly the shame of the cross.

For consider him that endured such: An amplification, taken from the circumstance of the person and the things themselves, which he compares between themselves: for how great is Jesus in comparison of us, and how far more grievous things did he suffer than we?

Ye have not yet resisted unto: He takes an argument from the profit which comes to us by God's chastisements, unless we are at fault. First of all because sin, or that rebellious wickedness of our flesh, is by this means tamed.

And ye have forgotten the exhortation: Secondly, because they are testimonies of his fatherly good will towards us, in that they show themselves to be illegitimate, if they cannot abide to be chastened by God.

Furthermore we have had fathers of: Thirdly, if all men yield this right to fathers, to whom next after God we owe this life, that they may rightfully correct their children, shall we not be much more subject to our Father, who is the author of spiritual and everlasting life?

For they verily for a few: An amplification of the same argument: Those fathers have corrected us after their fancy, for some frail and temporary good: but God chastens and instructs us for our singular good to make us partakers of his holiness: which although our senses do not presently perceive it, yet the end of the matter proves it.
Wherefore lift up the hands which: The conclusion: we must go forward courageously and keep always a right course and (as far forth as we may) without any staggering or stumbling.
hang down: The description of a man that is out of heart and completely discouraged.
straight paths for your feet: Keep a right course, and so, that you show examples of good life for others to follow.
Follow peace with all men: We must live in peace and holiness with all men.
Looking diligently lest any man fail: We must study to edify one another both in doctrine and example of life.
root of bitterness springing up trouble: That no heresy, or backsliding be an offence.

Lest there be any fornicator: We must shun immorality, and a profane mind, that is, such a mind as does not give God his due honour, which wickedness, how severely God will at length punish, the horrible example of Esau teaches us.

place of repentance: There was no room left for his repentance: and it appears by the effects, what his repentance really was, for when he left his father's presence, he threatened to kill his brother.

For ye are not come unto: Now he applies the same exhortation to the prophetic and kingly office of Christ compared with Moses, after this sort. If the majesty of the law was so great, how great do you think the glory of Christ and the gospel is? This comparison he declares also particularly.
touched: Which might be touched with hands, which was of a gross and earthly matter.
sight: The shape and form which he saw, which was no counterfeit and forged shape, but a true one.
perfect: So he calls them that are taken up to heaven, although one part of them sleeps in the earth.
See that ye refuse not him: The applying of the former comparison: If it were not lawful to condemn his word which was spoken on the earth, how much less his voice which is from heaven?

Whose voice then shook the earth: He compares the steadfast majesty of the gospel, with which the whole world was shaken, and even the very frame of heaven was astonished, with the small and vanishing sound of the governance by the law.
Yet once more I shake not: It appears evidently in this that the prophet speaks of the calling of the Gentiles, that these words must refer to the kingdom of Christ.

Wherefore we receiving a kingdom which: A general exhortation to live reverently and religiously under the most happy subjection of so mighty a King, who as he blesses his most mightily, so does he most severely revenge the rebellious. This is the sum of a Christian life, respecting the first table of the law.
reverence and godly: By reverence is meant that honest modesty which keeps them in their duties.
fear: Religious and godly fear.
